newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kubo says not set on continuing income tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: Kubo says not set on continuing income tax cuts.

text.p: Japan's special income tax cuts should not necessarily be continued into the next fiscal year, Finance Minister Wataru Kubo told a news conference on Wednesday.

"For fiscal 1997-98 we would like to look at the economic conditions and our goal to restructure state finances before making a final decision (on the income tax cuts). However, I do not necessarily hold the view that this measure must continue," he said.
The special income tax cuts, worth about two trillion yen annually, have been in place since fiscal 1994-95 with the aim of boosting the economy.
Kubo said Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the ministry's International Finance Bureau, may meet senior U.S. Trade representative Ira Shapiro later today in Washington.
However, Kubo said he had not received reports that the two would discuss a Japan-U.S. dispute on the insurance industry.
"There is no formal schedule that has been set for resuming bilateral insurance talks for now," he said.
Japan and the United States agreed last month to resume negotiations sometime after September 2.
"I would like to receive reports from Sakakibara on his return and give necessary instructions (on resuming the talks)," he said.
Sakakibara is in Washington to attend an Inter-American Development Bank conference.
